interpretationRules: In official challenge documentation, SI is defined as Super Intelligence. This catalog provides sourced flight research data; live SI/API evaluation is configured as an independent analysis module.
Investigation relevance ranking is not a universal ranking of flammability, absolute mission risk, or sole extinguishing agent performance.
Oxygen percentage alone does not constitute an equivalent atmosphere: total cabin pressure, diluent gas, forced airflow velocity, geometry, and fuel specimen must be cross-examined together.
In NASA PSI metadata, Completion Status reflects overall project status. FLEX 'Test end / Completion' is an experimental outcome tag; neither automatically signifies successful fire suppression.
Unspecified fields are left blank or explicitly qualified as unverified; planned or target flight conditions are never presented as measured test readouts.
NASA archival abstracts, calibrated sensor telemetry, editorial interpretations, numerical CFD outputs, and 3D architectural illustrations represent distinct evidence classes.
Clickable components in the Destiny US Lab model correlate to flight experiment disciplines; they do not represent exact chemical bills of materials for specific rack hardware.
3D flame and smoke visualizations inside the module are illustrative physics renderings, not fully validated CFD or spatial trajectory replays.
The Space Apps challenge explicitly notes a partial-gravity empirical data gap within PSI. LUCI is published simulated lunar-g research, and FM² represents planned lunar surface science.
Overheating smoke aerosol sensor readouts do not inherently constitute pre-labeled training benchmarks for autonomous anomaly prognosis without qualification.

comparisons.question: How do flame spread dynamics change across identical fuels when geometry, specimen dimensions, and flow rate vary?
comparisons.guard: Cross-examine material, ambient atmosphere, forced flow, and scale; do not convert multi-scale spread rates into a single flammability score.

comparisons.question: What is the measured effect of varying concurrent airflow across large-scale fabric specimens?
comparisons.guard: Verify actual flight telemetry timelines and sensor measurement definitions.

comparisons.question: How do particulate aging and source material composition alter optical smoke detector response curves?
comparisons.guard: Correlate sensor model, thermal profile, flow rate, and particle aging; do not interpret raw scattering voltage as particulate mass concentration.

comparisons.question: How do oxygen mole fraction, cabin pressure, and inert diluent composition govern droplet extinction limits?
comparisons.guard: Differentiate radiative extinction from technical test termination; normalize fuel droplet initial diameter and dilution ratios.

comparisons.question: Which flight investigation provides empirical evidence for specific spacecraft habitat fire safety layers?
comparisons.guard: Do not conflate distinct physical sensor metrics into an arbitrary composite safety score.

investigations.name: Saffire-I
investigations.objective: Investigate flame growth and propagation across large solid fabric specimens in microgravity.
fuels: SIBAL: cotton/fiberglass composite fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass blend)
geometry: Planar fabric sample approximately 40.6 × 94 cm
conditions: Forced convective channel flow
Fixed test chamber geometry; programmed airflow velocities and igniter firing intervals
measurements: Specimen surface and duct gas thermocouples
Calibrated O2/CO2, airflow, and igniter current channels in local Sample 1 dataset
investigations.platform: Uncrewed Cygnus vehicle post-unberth from ISS
investigations.relevance: Flame spread at realistic spacecraft interior scales; essential benchmark for convective and thermal transport models.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Conducted aboard uncrewed Cygnus, not inside the pressurized ISS US Lab cabin.
Igniter current initiation does not mark the exact moment of sustained flame propagation.
Pre-ignition quiescent recordings do not represent spontaneous anomaly prediction datasets.
A single sample test does not establish universal material flammability rankings.

localEvidence.sampling: 20,000 raw recordings; 0–659.967 s; approximately 33 ms intervals

events.label: First log record with fan power commanded off

localEvidence.note: Replays recorded flight sensor and fan states; not an empirical flame boundary mask for 3D simulation.

observedFinding.text: In concurrent flame spread, flame dimensions stabilized following initial ignition transients, contrasting sharply with accelerated upward buoyant burning on Earth.
observedFinding.scope: Large SIBAL sample under documented Saffire-I flow velocities; not universally generalizable to all cabin configurations.

investigations.name: Saffire-II
investigations.objective: Evaluate microgravity flammability limits of diverse solid samples and compare results with standard 1g flammability tests.
fuels: Multiple solid materials including PMMA acrylic, Nomex, and silicone sheets
geometry: Discrete sample cards mounted in sequential ignition carousel
conditions: Regulated duct airflow under microgravity conditions
measurements: Multispectral video, temperature profiles, atmospheric composition
investigations.platform: Uncrewed Cygnus vehicle post-unberth from ISS
investigations.relevance: Compares material flammability across matched atmospheric flow envelopes and elucidates geometric scale effects.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Tests conducted in Cygnus post-unberth; uncrewed conditions allowed full-burn assessments.
NASA-STD-6001 upward flame test comparison requires normalization for microgravity duct speed.

observedFinding.text: Demonstrated that certain materials self-extinguishing in standard Earth tests sustain continuous smoldering or steady propagation under low-speed microgravity airflow.
observedFinding.scope: Saffire-II sample card suite and ventilation conditions.

investigations.name: BASS
investigations.objective: Examine microgravity flame spread across solid fuels and evaluate gaseous nitrogen extinguishing effectiveness.
fuels: Cast and clear PMMA rods, flat sheets, and Nomex fabric
geometry: Rods (spherical/cylindrical geometry) and flat fuel strips
conditions: Low-speed forced airflow duct inside MSG
Nitrogen inerting injection

investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Small-scale samples constrained by glovebox containment safety limits.
Nitrogen dilution velocities require correction for glovebox recirculating dynamics.

observedFinding.text: In the absence of buoyancy, gaseous nitrogen injection successfully quenches flame propagation primarily by cooling the fuel surface and displacing ambient oxygen.

Replicated specimen runs capture test iterations rather than independent novel materials.

observedFinding.text: At extremely low air velocities (< 5 cm/s), radiative heat loss dominates over convective heat gain, resulting in a low-speed quenching boundary.

investigations.name: SAME
investigations.objective: Characterize smoke particulate size distributions and verify optical detector responses from overheating spacecraft materials.
fuels: Teflon-insulated wire, Kapton polyimide, silicone rubber, pyrolysis cellulose
geometry: Heated wire coils and furnace aerosol generation canisters
conditions: Controlled thermal ramp (pyrolysis without open flaming)
Variable particulate aging times
investigations.relevance: Provides foundational physics for pre-fire smoke detection and detector sensor selection in spacecraft life support loops.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Controlled pyrolysis heating; does not simulate high-energy electrical arcing or explosive ignition.
Sensor voltage output must be analyzed against aerosol morphology rather than raw volume.

observedFinding.text: Microgravity pyrolysis produces significantly larger agglomerated smoke particulates than Earth 1g tests due to the absence of buoyant break-up and extended agglomeration times.

investigations.name: FLEX
investigations.objective: Measure combustion and extinction limits of isolated liquid fuel droplets and assess gaseous suppressant efficiency.
fuels: Methanol, heptane, decane, and alcohol-alkane blended fuel droplets
geometry: Free and tethered isolated spherical droplets (1.5–5.0 mm initial diameter)
conditions: Variable ambient pressures (0.5–3.0 atm)
Oxygen fractions from 12% to 40%
Inert diluents (N2, CO2, He, Xe)
investigations.facility: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in CIR
investigations.relevance: Primary reference database for droplet burning rates, extinction diameters, and inert dilution suppression physics.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Distinguishes between complete burn, diffusive extinction, and droplet disruption events.
Tethered fiber conducts minor heat; tether-free runs validate spherical symmetry.

observedFinding.text: Demonstrated that carbon dioxide is significantly more effective per mole than nitrogen in suppressing droplet combustion due to its higher molar heat capacity and radiative re-absorption.

geometry: Dual-droplet linear arrays and single suspended droplets
conditions: Slow convective drift and quiescent inerted atmospheres
measurements: Inter-droplet distance, flame merger boundaries, burning rate constants
investigations.relevance: Advances spray combustion safety models and mutual interaction dynamics between adjacent burning fuel sites.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.

investigations.name: ACME
investigations.objective: Host six microgravity gaseous combustion investigations within a shared modular chamber to advance fire safety and clean energy.
fuels: Methane, ethylene, propane, and diluted hydrogen gas mixtures
geometry: Porous spherical and co-flow burners
conditions: Microgravity quiescent and co-flow environments
Applied electrostatic potentials up to 5 kV
measurements: Chemiluminescence, laser diagnostics, soot volume fractions
investigations.relevance: Overarching research program providing fundamental data on gas burner stability, electric field soot control, and material flammability.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: ACME is a multi-investigation umbrella program; distinct sub-experiments address different combustion aspects.

observedFinding.text: Supplying electric fields to microgravity flames induces ion wind body forces that modify flame geometry, suppress soot emission, and alter flammability boundaries without physical containment walls.

investigations.name: BRE — Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.objective: Investigate extinction limits of solid materials burning in a stagnation-plate flow geometry.
fuels: Cast and extruded PMMA polymer discs
geometry: Stagnation surface flow impinging on flat fuel samples
conditions: Controlled oxygen concentration and stagnation blow-off velocities
measurements: Critical heat flux, flame stand-off, extinction oxygen index
investigations.relevance: Directly models flammability thresholds and extinction airflow limits relevant to spacecraft material acceptance standards.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Disc geometry focuses on stagnation point flow; complementary to channel flow tests.

observedFinding.text: Determined that microgravity materials extinguish at lower forced velocities than predicted by 1g downward flammability standards.

investigations.name: CLD Flame
investigations.objective: Investigate the structure, stability, and liftoff dynamics of co-flow lifted laminar gas flames.
fuels: Diluted methane and ethylene gases
Inert nitrogen-diluted fuel blends
geometry: Co-flow laminar jet burner with lifted flame stabilization zone
conditions: Regulated fuel injection velocity
Variable co-flow oxidizer velocities
investigations.relevance: Advances gravity-independent combustion models, flame stabilization physics, and computational burner validation.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Fundamental gas burner experiment; not a direct solid spacecraft material flammability test.

observedFinding.text: Demonstrated that without buoyant acceleration, lifted laminar flames stabilize farther downstream, exhibiting broader reaction zones.

investigations.name: E-FIELD Flames
investigations.objective: Determine the effects of DC electric fields on microgravity gas flames to understand ion-driven body forces and soot control.
fuels: Sub-experiment gaseous hydrocarbons including methane and ethylene
geometry: Laminar gas burner with surrounding mesh high-voltage electrode
conditions: Applied DC electric fields from 0 to 5 kV in microgravity
Quiescent and co-flow arrangements
Field-induced chemi-ion drift
investigations.relevance: Pioneers active electrostatic flame control and suppression mechanisms for hermetically sealed space cabins.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Electric field body forces simulate effective acceleration on ions; they do not reproduce actual lunar or Martian gravity.
Laboratory demonstration; not an operational certified electrostatic spacecraft fire extinguisher.

observedFinding.text: Electrostatic forces acting on chemi-ions deform spherical microgravity flames into conical shapes, extracting soot particles and enhancing convective cooling.

investigations.name: Flame Design
investigations.objective: Examine soot formation and control in microgravity diffusion flames through stoichiometric dilution and burner design.
fuels: Diluted hydrocarbon gases (ethylene, methane) with inert additives
geometry: Inverse and standard co-flow diffusion burners
conditions: Microgravity ambient with controlled oxygen and diluent ratios
measurements: Soot concentration, radiative heat transfer, spectral emission
investigations.relevance: Improves early particulate detection strategies and clean combustion design for spacecraft thrusters and life support heaters.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Focuses on gaseous diffusion flames; provides indirect physical context for solid cable smoke.

observedFinding.text: Stoichiometrically diluted inverse flames eliminate incandescent soot emission while maintaining stable low-temperature reaction envelopes.

investigations.name: s-Flame
investigations.objective: Investigate the structure, stability, and extinction transitions of spherical gas diffusion flames.
fuels: Porous sphere supplied with hydrogen, methane, or ethylene
geometry: Spherical porous metal burner (6.4 mm diameter)
conditions: Quiescent microgravity cabin atmospheres with variable diluents
measurements: Flame radius, radiation loss, extinction temperature
investigations.relevance: Fundamental physics for 1D spherical combustion and radiative extinction modeling in enclosed environments.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Spherical symmetry represents an idealized laboratory boundary condition.

observedFinding.text: Spherical diffusion flames in microgravity undergo abrupt radiative extinction when the heat radiated to cold chamber walls exceeds chemical heat release.

investigations.name: CFI-G — Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.objective: Establish and observe low-temperature 'cool flame' regimes in microgravity gaseous hydrocarbon fuels.
fuels: Alkane gas mixtures with ozone/oxygen sensitization
geometry: Porous spherical and jet burners
conditions: Low-temperature reaction regimes (600–900 K) in microgravity
measurements: UV chemiluminescence, formaldehyde emission, micro-thermocouple probes
investigations.relevance: Critical safety insight showing that visual disappearance of hot flame does not guarantee total combustion cessation.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Cool flames produce negligible visible light; requires UV/IR radiometer diagnostics.

observedFinding.text: Confirmed that gaseous cool flames can burn stably without buoyancy, presenting a silent, invisible combustion hazard requiring multi-spectral optical detectors.

investigations.name: CFI — Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.objective: Investigate low-temperature combustion dynamics and secondary cool flame regimes in free-floating liquid fuel droplets.
fuels: Large alkane droplets (n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane)
geometry: Isolated free-floating liquid spheres
conditions: Quiescent microgravity with standard and oxygen-enriched atmospheres
measurements: OH* and CH* emission, droplet diameter tracking, gas-phase pyrometry
investigations.relevance: Redefines spacecraft fire extinction protocols by proving secondary low-temperature burning can persist after hot flame quenching.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Requires high-sensitivity camera integration to distinguish from true total extinction.

observedFinding.text: Following hot flame extinction, droplets re-ignite into invisible cool flames driven by low-temperature chain-branching chemistry, continuing until all liquid fuel is consumed.

investigations.name: DAFT
investigations.objective: Verify operational reliability and calibration fidelity of aerosol particle sizing instrumentation in microgravity.
fuels: Pre-characterized test aerosols and condensation nuclei
geometry: Instrument calibration flow path
conditions: Operational validation in zero-gravity cabin flow
measurements: Particle count accuracy, fluidic condensation efficiency
investigations.relevance: Validates diagnostic instruments and particle counters required for autonomous spacecraft smoke detection systems.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Instrument verification experiment; does not generate standalone material flammability curves.

observedFinding.text: Validated that condensation nucleus counters maintain sample air saturation and reliable sizing without gravity-assisted drainage.

investigations.name: DAFT-2
investigations.objective: Test modified P-Trak condensation nucleus counter performance and fluid dynamics across extended ISS flight operations.
fuels: Controlled aerosol generation sources
geometry: Airflow sampling duct
conditions: Microgravity cabin ambient sampling
measurements: Condensation particle concentration, alcohol wick longevity
investigations.relevance: Supports flight qualification of high-reliability smoke detectors for long-duration deep space exploration missions.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: DAFT and DAFT-2 share accession records under PSI-47; represents instrumentation qualification.

observedFinding.text: Demonstrated alcohol fluid storage stability in microgravity wicks, ensuring uninterrupted particle counting during prolonged emergency scenarios.

investigations.name: SPICE — Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment
investigations.objective: Determine the smoke point threshold where soot escapes from microgravity co-flow laminar diffusion flames.
fuels: Gaseous hydrocarbons (methane, propane, ethylene)
geometry: Co-flow jet diffusion flame
conditions: Constant airflow with incrementally increased fuel injection rate
measurements: Luminous flame height, smoke point flow threshold, video imaging
investigations.relevance: Quantifies the boundary between contained soot burning and external smoke emission, critical for optical detector placement.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Smoke point marks the onset of soot emission; does not measure total chemical gas toxicity.

observedFinding.text: In microgravity, longer molecular residence times enhance soot agglomeration, causing flames to emit smoke at lower fuel flow rates than identical burners in 1g.

investigations.name: SLICE — Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
investigations.objective: Investigate laminar gas flame structure, flame tip liftoff, and blowout limits using the SPICE hardware.
fuels: Gaseous hydrocarbon fuels
geometry: Co-flow laminar burner
conditions: Constant fuel flow with incrementally stepped co-flow air velocity
measurements: Photographic records, liftoff distance, blowout airflow velocity
investigations.relevance: Fundamental science for flow-driven fire stabilization, flame detachment, and blowout extinguishing limits.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Liftoff is flame base detachment from burner rim; distinct from complete extinction.

observedFinding.text: Microgravity flames lift off cleanly from the burner port at lower air velocities due to the absence of buoyant base recirculation, stabilizing downstream before blowing out.

investigations.name: LUCI — Lunar Combustion Investigation
investigations.objective: Investigate solid fuel flammability and flame spread under simulated lunar partial gravity aboard a spinning suborbital vehicle.
fuels: PMMA acrylic cylinders and flat solid fuel samples
geometry: 4 mm diameter cylindrical polymer rods and flat slabs
conditions: Simulated 1/6 g partial gravity via centrifuge rotation during rocket freefall
Atmospheric air pressure
measurements: Dual orthogonal cameras, oxygen concentration, regression rate
investigations.relevance: Provides published experimental evidence bridging the partial-gravity knowledge gap between microgravity (0g) and Moon gravity (0.16g).
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Conducted in centrifuge rotation during suborbital flight, not on the actual lunar surface.
Results require qualification when extrapolating to elevated oxygen Artemis habitats.

observedFinding.text: Observed that flame spread rates in simulated 0.16g lunar gravity exceeded microgravity spread rates due to the re-emergence of weak buoyant convective drafts.

investigations.name: FM² — Flammability of Materials on the Moon
investigations.objective: Establish empirical flammability boundaries and ignition thresholds for solid spacecraft materials on the lunar surface.
fuels: Artemis habitat polymer materials, Nomex, Kapton, and composite wire insulation
geometry: Standardized flat specimen cards and cylindrical wiring geometries
conditions: Authentic 1/6 g lunar surface gravity
Artemis exploration atmospheres (56 kPa, 34% O2)
measurements: Direct surface regression rate, limiting oxygen concentration, thermal radiative flux
investigations.relevance: Target flight research identified to resolve the empirical lunar partial-gravity flammability paradox for the Artemis program.
investigations.relevanceType: source-grounded editorial interpretation; not a measured safety score
investigations.habitatApplicability: Research findings guide safety design and simulation models; not a standalone flight hardware material certification.
limitations: Planned research benchmark; empirical flight data pending future lunar payload mission.
Serves as the defined forward-looking data gap in the NASA Space Apps Challenge roadmap.

observedFinding.text: Identified in challenge scope as the essential next-generation empirical validation required to certify materials for pressurized lunar habitats.
observedFinding.scope: FM² planned Artemis lunar surface mission.
